entities.summary:
The Anarchy, spanning 1135-1153, was a period of civil war that ravaged England and Normandy. This tumultuous era emerged in the throes of succession disputes and power struggles between the British monarchy and the powerful nobility. At its core, the Anarchy was a clash of wills between King Stephen of Blois, Stephen of England, and Empress Matilda, who vied for control of the English throne.

The Anarchy saw the rise of powerful barons, who exploited the power vacuum to expand their own territories and influence. This period also witnessed the growth of feudalism, as lords and vassals solidified their positions within the English nobility. As the Anarchy dragged on, England's economy and social fabric suffered greatly, with widespread violence, displacement, and economic hardship.

The Anarchy ultimately came to an end with the ascension of Henry II, who would go on to shape the course of English history and establish a strong centralized monarchy. The legacy of the Anarchy can still be seen in the complex web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that characterized the medieval period.

As one historian noted, 'The Anarchy was a time of unrelenting chaos, but it also laid the groundwork for the rise of a powerful English monarchy that would shape the course of Western history.'
